title: Missing Refresh Token Rotation - No Token Rotation on Refresh
description: The vulnerable API does not implement refresh token rotation. When a refresh token is used to obtain a new access token, the same refresh token is returned (or a new one is issued without revoking the old one). This allows a stolen refresh token to be used indefinitely until its natural expiration (7 days). The secure implementation (api-secure) implements refresh token rotation: each refresh generates a new refresh token and revokes the old one.
impact: Long-lived refresh token exposure. A stolen refresh token remains valid for its full lifetime (7 days) regardless of how many times it's used. An attacker with a stolen refresh token can maintain persistent access for the full token lifetime without detection.
mitigation: 1) Implement refresh token rotation: on each refresh, generate new refresh token and revoke the old one (store revokedAt timestamp). 2) Store refresh token hashes in RefreshTokenRepository with revokedAt field. 3) Check revokedAt on each refresh attempt. 4. Secure API (api-secure) implements rotation in RefreshTokenCommand.
